extracted.intended_audience: students and enthusiasts of mathematics (AoPS community)
extracted.subtask_description: A short reference article defining what counts as a mathematical convention (facts, names, notation, or usages generally agreed upon by mathematicians), why conventions exist, and notes on durability and competing usages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mathematical convention (core definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: A mathematical convention is a fact, name, notation, or usage which is generally agreed upon by mathematicians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the article's central definitional criterion. The page emphasizes that many aspects of mathematical language (names, symbols, orders of operations) are conventions rather than intrinsic truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose: shared understanding without redefinition
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians abide by conventions in order to allow other mathematicians to understand what they write without constantly having to redefine basic terms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives the example that if conventions did not exist, every paper might need to re-explain basics (e.g., PEMDAS), illustrating why conventions are adopted for communicative efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of things treated as conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Conventions can be facts, names, notation, or usages (e.g., order of operations, symbol choices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entry notes 'nearly all mathematical names and symbols are conventional,' indicating a broad scope — both semantic (names) and syntactic (notation/usages) items are covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longevity increases likelihood of becoming conventional
rubrics_metrics.description: The longer a name or notation has been in use, the more likely it is to become a mathematical convention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This expresses a descriptive criterion about how conventions form over time: widespread, long-standing usage tends to solidify into convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing conventions can prevent consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: Some notational questions stubbornly refuse to develop conventional solutions, usually because two or more competing conventions achieve wide-spread usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This warns that conventions are not guaranteed; when multiple widely-used conventions exist, no single standard may emerge (the page points to the 'Natural numbers' article as an example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate meaning: 'convention' as a gathering
rubrics_metrics.description: In English, a convention can also mean a place where people convene; thus 'mathematical convention' may refer to meetings whose purpose is mathematical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives Mu Alpha Theta's yearly gatherings as an example, clarifying a potential ambiguity in the phrase's usage.
